chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: Changing this base alone will not reproducibly produce a TF-dependent change in enhancer activity or target-gene expression; the association may reflect linkage or another mechanism.
The reported occupancy and in-vitro binding predictions will not translate into a variant-specific molecular effect in relevant liver cells.
falsified_if: Precise editing of G to T reproducibly changes enhancer activity or target-gene expression in relevant liver cells and the effect depends on a specific TF.

chains.title: Alt-enhanced CEBPA binding increases enhancer activity
chains.element: The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646; its reported activity scores are maxima across biosamples, not liver-specific measurements.
chains.target_gene: SORT1 is the strongest locus-level target candidate, but direct regulation of SORT1 by this cCRE is not shown.
chains.cell_type: A candidate effect in liver cells is supported by CEBPA occupancy in HepG2 and CEBPA expression in Hep 3B2.1-7.

links.claim: CEBPA is reported to occupy the site in HepG2, and QBiC-SELEX predicts stronger alt-T binding; importantly, E35 includes an alt-increasing CEBPA-specific model as well as a mapped CEBPB model, so the direction is not based only on the related-factor model.
The variant lies in the distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646, although the reported chromatin activity maxima are not liver-specific.
SORT1 is a leading candidate target based on locus-to-gene scores and an alt-increasing liver eQTL, but these data do not connect this cCRE directly to SORT1.
CEBPA occupancy in HepG2 and its high expression in Hep 3B2.1-7 support, but do not establish, a liver-cell mechanism.

An alt-associated increase in SORT1 is directionally compatible with the alt-increasing liver eQTL and the predominantly G-risk cholesterol associations; mediation to cholesterol traits or myocardial infarction is not established.

predictions: An allele-specific assay should show stronger CEBPA binding to T than G; reducing CEBPA should reduce the T-versus-G difference in enhancer activity if CEBPA mediates it.
If CEBPA activates this element, precise G-to-T editing should increase SORT1 expression, provided this cCRE regulates SORT1 in the tested liver cells.
falsified_if: A well-controlled allele-specific assay finds no CEBPA preference for T, or CEBPA perturbation leaves the variant-dependent enhancer effect unchanged.
Precise editing produces no reproducible variant-dependent molecular effect in a relevant liver-cell assay.

chains.title: Loss of ref-preferred KLF6 binding relieves enhancer repression
chains.element: The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646; its liver-specific activity is not established.
chains.target_gene: SORT1 is the leading locus-level target candidate, but direct regulation by this cCRE is not shown.
chains.cell_type: KLF6 occupancy in HepG2 and expression in Hep 3B2.1-7 support a candidate liver-cell mechanism.

links.claim: KLF6 is reported to occupy the variant in HepG2, and its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger ref-G binding at a strong site; this does not establish allele-specific occupancy in cells.
The variant lies in the distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646, with activity-associated chromatin scores reported across biosamples rather than specifically in liver.
SORT1 is a candidate target based on its high locus-to-gene support and positive liver eQTL for T, but the evidence does not link this cCRE directly to SORT1.
KLF6 occupancy in HepG2 and expression in Hep 3B2.1-7 support a candidate liver-cell role.

If KLF6 represses this element, reduced binding on T could be consistent with increased liver SORT1 expression and the cholesterol-association direction, but repression and trait mediation are not demonstrated.

predictions: An allele-specific assay should show stronger KLF6 binding to G; KLF6 depletion should preferentially relieve repression on G if this TF is the mediator.
KLF6 perturbation should affect the allele-dependent enhancer effect, unlike a model mediated by MLX or CEBPA.
falsified_if: KLF6 lacks a ref-G preference in an allele-specific assay, or KLF6 perturbation leaves the variant-dependent effect unchanged.
KLF6 activates rather than represses the element and no alternative mechanism explains the proposed direction.

chains.title: Loss of ref-preferred MLX binding relieves enhancer repression
chains.element: The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646; liver-specific activity is not provided.
chains.target_gene: SORT1 is a candidate target from locus-level evidence, but this cCRE has not been directly linked to it.
chains.cell_type: MLX occupancy in HepG2 and expression in Hep 3B2.1-7 support a candidate liver-cell mechanism.

links.claim: MLX is reported to occupy the variant in HepG2, and its QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger binding to ref G at a strong site; this is an in-vitro binding prediction, not allele-specific occupancy.
The site is within the distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646, whose reported activity scores are across biosamples.
SORT1 is a candidate target based on locus-to-gene scores and an alt-increasing liver eQTL, but direct regulation by this cCRE remains unshown.
MLX occupancy in HepG2 and expression in Hep 3B2.1-7 support a candidate liver-cell setting.
If MLX represses the element, loss of its binding on T could fit the liver eQTL and cholesterol-association direction; MLX repression and mediation to the trait are not established.

predictions: An allele-specific assay should show stronger MLX binding to G; MLX depletion should preferentially relieve repression on G if the proposed repressor model is correct.
MLX perturbation should change the allele-dependent enhancer effect; this dependence distinguishes the model from the CEBPA and KLF6 models.
falsified_if: MLX lacks a ref-G binding preference in a relevant allele-specific assay, or MLX perturbation does not affect the variant-dependent effect.
MLX activates rather than represses the element and no alternative mechanism explains the proposed direction.

chains.title: Loss of ref-preferred HNF4A binding changes enhancer repression
chains.element: The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646; its liver-specific activity has not been established.
chains.target_gene: SORT1 is a plausible locus-level target, but regulation of SORT1 by this cCRE is unproven.
chains.cell_type: HNF4A occupancy in HepG2 and expression in Hep 3B2.1-7 make a liver-cell mechanism plausible.

links.claim: HNF4A is reported bound at the site; its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts a modest ref-G preference, whereas the stronger alt-increasing signal comes from an NR2F2-mapped model and does not establish HNF4A's allele preference.
The variant lies in the distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646, with activity-associated chromatin scores reported across biosamples rather than specifically in liver.
SORT1 is supported as a locus-level candidate by L2G scores and an alt-increasing liver eQTL, but direct cCRE-to-SORT1 regulation is not shown.
HNF4A occupancy in HepG2 and expression in Hep 3B2.1-7 support a candidate liver-cell setting.

If ref-preferred HNF4A represses this element, reduced binding on T could be consistent with increased liver SORT1 expression and the cholesterol association direction, but neither repression nor trait mediation is demonstrated.

predictions: An HNF4A-specific allele-binding assay should show a ref preference, and HNF4A perturbation should alter the G-versus-T enhancer effect if HNF4A mediates it.
Under the proposed repressor model, HNF4A depletion should preferentially relieve repression on G and reduce the expression difference between alleles.
falsified_if: An HNF4A-specific assay finds no ref preference and HNF4A perturbation does not affect the allele-dependent enhancer effect.
HNF4A is shown to activate rather than repress this element, with no alternative account of the proposed direction.

Hepatic expression of PSRC1-CELSR2-SORT1 protects against CHD via RC reduction, independent of LDL-C, supporting RC as promising target for CHD prevention.

Sortilin (encoded by SORT1), a multi-ligand intracellular trafficking receptor, has recently emerged as a critical molecular mediator linking metabolic risk factors-such as dyslipidemia, diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease-to pro-calcific cellular responses.

GWASs and sequencing studies have identified key genetic variations associated with CAD, including JCAD/KIAA1462, GUCY1A3, PCSK9, and SORT1, which regulate inflammation, lipid metabolism, and vascular function.

The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
